howto.name: Add your images
howto.text: Drop or select JPG images; each one becomes a page, in the order shown.

howto.name: Arrange the pages
howto.text: Put the images in the order you want the pages to appear before converting.

howto.name: Choose a page size
howto.text: Auto (the default) makes every page exactly the size of its image. A4 and Letter place each image on a standard page instead, which prints predictably.

howto.name: Create the PDF
howto.text: Convert and download a single PDF containing all the images, one per page. Photos a phone stored sideways are turned upright, as the phone shows them. Location and camera details (EXIF, XMP and IPTC metadata) are removed. Each photo is copied into the PDF without re-encoding; the rare JPEG that can't be copied as it is, such as a lossless one, is stored from its decoded pixels instead.

faq.q: Which page size should I choose?
faq.a: Auto keeps each page the shape of its image, which is ideal for viewing on screen. Choose A4 or Letter when the PDF will be printed or submitted somewhere that expects standard pages; the images are fitted onto the page.

faq.q: Can I combine many images into one PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Every image you add becomes a page of the same PDF, in the order shown — the usual way to turn photos of a multi-page document into a single file.

No detail is removed on purpose: each photo is placed in the PDF at its full resolution and scaled on the page to fit. That also means large photos produce a large PDF; run Compress PDF afterwards if you need it smaller.
This page takes JPG. Image to PDF accepts other common formats, such as PNG and WebP, with the same page-size options.

faq.q: Is there a limit on image size?
faq.a: Very large images are rejected rather than processed, to protect the server's memory; normal photos and scans are far below that limit. One PDF can take up to 100 images with a combined size of up to 200 MB, which is roughly 50 phone photos; convert the rest as a second PDF.

faq.q: Can I make the text in my photographed pages searchable?
faq.a: Not in this step — a PDF of photos is just pictures. Run OCR PDF on the result to add a searchable text layer.

faq.q: What happens to my images after I upload them?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and converted on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, using local libraries rather than a third-party service. Response cleanup removes the images and the PDF and the result after your download is sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is added to an account or file library.
